observations.value: Decision (accepted Oct 15, 2026): on LXD 6.x servers that offer auth_bearer (tested on 6.9), a bearer identity works as the plugin client credential for the remote API, with the same groups and effective permissions as a TLS identity; LXD 5.21 has no bearer identities. Client certificates stay the default; a bearer token is optional, read from a file that the plugin re-reads when it changes and once after a 403 on GET /1.0, failing closed otherwise. Tokens are valid for 10 years unless issued with an expiry, so the documentation requires an explicit short expiry; LXD refuses an expired token at once with 403 on every path, GET /1.0 included, and issuing a new token revokes the previous one immediately, so rotation is a cut-over: the issuing job writes the token file atomically right after issuing. Short-lived tokens move the long-lived privilege to whoever issues them (identity management rights), which the documentation states. Evidence: runs 20261013T191114Z-g-l13-*.
